statement: Let Z(x) be a smooth divergence-free field on a flat torus. Let σ be the smooth step which is zero for t ≤ 0, one for t ≥ 1, and satisfies σ(t) + σ(1 − t) = 1. Define α0(t) = σ(2t − 1), α1(t) = σ(2t − 1) 1 + t , u(t, x) = α(t)Z(x). For either choice α = α0, α1, the residual force is f = α′ Z + α2 (Z · ∇)Z − να∆Z. (9) It has bounded mixed derivatives, gives zero initial velocity and pressure zero, and follows the spatial flow of Z at the onto time s(t) = R t 0 α. For α0, s(t) = t − 3/4 for t ≥ 1, and the force is stationary there. For α1, s(t) = s(1) + log 1 + t 2 (t ≥ 1), and the force tends uniformly to zero and belongs to space-time L2. If R Z = 0, both forces have zero mean. In general their means equal α′ R Z.
